subject: MSA / Order Form — exposure ceiling alignment and carve-outs
messages:
From: Jordan Willis <jordan.willis@acme.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — exposure ceiling & carve-out alignment

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement and legal asked us to send our standard redlines for the MSA and the attached order form so we can align on limits and exclusions before your legal team sends a counter. Two quick items they flagged up front:

- Limitation of liability: procurement is pushing to cap exposure at 1x fees paid under the order form; they prefer a rolling 12-month calculation.
- Consequential damages: they want a broad waiver but are open to carve-outs for security/data incidents that impact customers.

I've attached our annotated MSA (acme_redline_msa.docx) and the questionnaire. Can your team propose a practical path to closure here? We have internal timelines — procurement needs final language by end of next week to make the Q2 purchase window.

Appreciate it,
Jordan Willis
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Cloud

Attachment: acme_redline_msa.docx (redlined MSA)
Attachment: acme_procurement_questionnaire.pdf (procurement checklist)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Willis <jordan.willis@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — exposure ceiling & carve-out alignment

Jordan — thanks for sending these over and for the clear ask and timing. Looping in Laura (legal) and Markus (finance) so we can converge on both legal and commercial tradeoffs.

High level — we typically propose one of two pragmatic approaches for enterprise order forms:

Option A (annualized cap):
- Limit equals the fees paid under the order form during the preceding 12 months (resets annually on the anniversary).
- Multipliers only for security/data breaches that are our fault: up to 2x annual fees.

Option B (contract-term aggregate):
- Single aggregate cap equal to 3x total fees paid over the contract term (no reset).
- Narrowly carved-out liabilities (willful misconduct, breaches of confidentiality, IP indemnity) remain outside the cap.

We believe Option A gives your procurement predictability while keeping risk aligned to annual spend; Option B helps Redwood when customers prepay or commit multi-year credits.

Next steps: Laura — can you propose redline language for both options and call out specific carve-outs we cannot accept (e.g., unlimited consequential carve-outs across the board)? Markus — please flag any commercial constraints if we move to 1x vs 3x approaches.

I can coordinate a 30-minute sync tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: proposed_option_summaries.pdf (internal)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — exposure ceiling alignment and carve-outs

Folks — I reviewed Acme's redline and the two options Stephanie outlined. Key legal positions and suggested language below (high-level):

1) Cap basis: we can accept a 12-month rolling fees calculation, but our legal preference is to define the measurement period precisely as "Fees actually invoiced and collected by Redwood under the applicable Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the date of the claim." This avoids disputes over credits/unused prepay.

2) Multipliers & severity buckets: we can propose a tiered approach —
- Security/data breach resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct: cap = 3x prior 12 months' fees, subject to proof of direct damages.
- All other covered claims: cap = 1x prior 12 months' fees.

3) Carve-outs: we will push to keep the standard carve-outs (willful misconduct, bodily injury, fraud, IP indemnity) outside the cap. We will not broadly accept an indefinite consequential-damages carve-out tied to third-party integrations or partner outages — that's too expansive. We can accept limited consequential carve-outs where there is a demonstrable direct customer impact tied to Redwood's security control failures.

4) Annual reset vs aggregate: prefer an annual reset for customers that purchase recurring SaaS seats or subscriptions. For customers who prepay large multi-year credits, we'll accept an aggregate cap tied to total paid amounts but request a commercially higher multiplier.

I'll draft concrete redline snippets for Option A and Option B and upload to the Drive link. Flagging potential negotiation risk: Acme's ask for a flat 1x total-fees (with no carve-outs) is unlikely to be acceptable to Redwood without compensation (price or limited indemnity).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts 
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — exposure ceiling alignment and carve-outs

Quick commercial input from finance:

- 1x rolling-12-month cap is acceptable only if Acme's order volume is relatively stable and they aren't front-loading a large prepay. If the order includes >60% upfront credit we should prefer aggregate 3x multiplier or apply a per-invoice pro-rata cap.
- From a deal economics standpoint, moving from 1x -> 2x for security incidents materially changes expected loss provisioning; anything above 3x gets into unacceptable tail risk without additional pricing.

If Laura's redlines can implement the measurement clarity (collected vs invoiced) and limit the security carve-out to "gross negligence or willful misconduct" we can make the pricing work. Also recommend we keep an explicit fallback: if dispute over measurement arises, parties will engage a neutral auditor to reconcile invoiced vs collected.

Markus Klein
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Willis <jordan.willis@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@acme.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 14:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — exposure ceiling alignment and carve-outs

Stephanie and team — thanks for the fast responses. A few clarifications from our side after a procurement/legal review:

- Procurement will not accept aggregate caps that significantly exceed 1x unless there's a commercial offset (discount reduction or a security SLA credit). Their mandate is to keep liability aligned with annual spend.
- They are open to a 2x multiplier for confirmed data breaches that result from Redwood's proven willful misconduct, but anything above 2x is a hard no for our CFO.
- On measurement: Acme prefers "fees paid" to avoid disputes about collection, but we can discuss language.

Next step from our side: I'll circulate an internal note to procurement and check whether we can accept the limited security carve-out language scoped to "gross negligence or willful misconduct". Procurement's timeline still expects final language by 23 May.

Jordan
Director, Strategic Sourcing, Acme Cloud

Attachment: acme_procurement_followup.pdf

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — exposure ceiling alignment and carve-outs

Jordan — appreciate the clarity and timeline. Summary and immediate asks: 

1) Laura will post two redline snippets to the Drive: Option A (12-month rolling cap with 2x for security willful/gross negligence) and Option B (aggregate 3x total-fees with narrower carve-outs).
2) Markus will model the economics of 1x vs 2x under the expected Acme purchase profile and call out any recommended price adjustments.
3) Jordan — if procurement can confirm whether "fees paid" vs "fees invoiced and collected" is a hard requirement, let us know; that will materially affect the measurement language.

Proposal: 30-minute sync Monday 21 May at 10am PT to review the redlines and converge on one approach before final counter. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and upload Laura's redlines to the HubSpot deal record.

Thanks all — moving to a 1:1 redline exchange should get this across the finish line quickly.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations
